findings.defect: seal derived changed_paths from Git cached stat data, so a worker could hide a protected-file or baseline-test modification with assume-unchanged/skip-worktree index flags or a same-size edit with the original mtime restored; the recorded changed_paths was never re-checked afterwards
findings.fix: sealing refuses nonstandard index entries, refreshes worktree stat data before diffing, compares symlink targets by blob object id, and check/review/receipt/accept recompute the change set and refuse when it differs from sealed.json; the receipt now carries the sealed changed_paths

findings.defect: the named-Go-test gate validated only the captured event stream, so a worker-supplied TestMain that printed fabricated run/pass frames and exited without m.Run() was accepted as named-test execution
findings.fix: for go-executable gates that declare go_tests and go_package the runner derives and executes go test -list in the gate directory and refuses unless the package's own test binary lists every named test exactly once; the runbook and review instructions state the residual limit and the reviewer duty

findings.defect: the delivered review record (and its embedded copy in the positive receipt) claimed that the object-shape check and the trailing-data guard were pinned by the 11 rejection inputs and that all 11 inputs reach the custom decoder; both claims were false
findings.fix: both texts now state which guards the inputs pin and which stay unobservable (non-object and field-missing inputs are subsumed by JSON type errors and Subject.Validate, no input carries trailing data, and the map decode ahead of ensureDecoderEOF already rejects it); review.json was normalized to the repository eol=lf convention (sha256:f60e306144790ff1af843433520b911a09a275c8fa46c6cbc3b67a15b7a2fb26) and the delivered positive receipt rebound (sha256:1fdf4aa86285c79d279657294016a4d01da362c2f8977c09c51b55d203090808, superseding the bound-revision copy 524e3beed5ccf310169400f27b21a6c73ab166814e49e43f7c925a159abceb24)

findings.defect: the exporter exported session-controlled record type names verbatim (a type name matching the runner secret-key pattern made the whole usage row unusable with a misleading refusal), asserted usage_includes_all_assistant_attempts unconditionally, and passed path-like session identifiers through raw
findings.fix: secret-like type names are counted under a sha256 key with an explicit limitation, the all-attempts claim is conditional on recognized record types and complete assistant identities, and path-like identifiers are hashed with limitation codes; a regression test binds an exported row through the runner six-stage validate_usage

findings.defect: runner robustness and accounting gaps: accounting_complete could be true with both cost totals null; deep or non-UTF-8 values raised uncaught tracebacks after validation; junction directories were traversed outside the checkout; slashless protected patterns did not match nested paths; --timeout accepted negatives; docstrings misstated the review binding and the manifest scope
findings.fix: explicit unknown-cost reasons per channel, serialization and path-encoding refusals, reparse-point directory refusal, gitignore-style slashless patterns, negative-timeout refusal, and corrected docstrings, each with a regression test

findings.defect: audit and document reconciliation gaps: resolved dispositions carried review-time values that contradicted the delivered receipts, a disposition pointed at a non-existent remaining_blockers field, the unversioned-estimate subtotal omitted the open coordinator prefix, the evidence record claimed no commit was performed and no executable source changed after the reviewed 20-case gate, and the review instructions requested a non-schema reviewed-paths field
findings.fix: dispositions updated to the final values, references point at retained_nonblocking_limits, the estimate labels separate the completed-session subtotal from the open prefix, the delivery commit and later repair increments are stated explicitly, and the review instructions match the strict record schema

retained_nonblocking_limits: Incomplete provider billing/prices, unreported helpers/transport usage and post-cutoff coordinator tail remain unknown, never zero.
Separate same-family reviewer invocation is not model-family diversity.
No OS sandbox, hostile same-user evidence protection, append-only history or transient in-gate edit detection is claimed.
Interrupted attempt stores and abnormal validator-process records remain fail-closed, preserved and not automatically resumable.
Executable-mode branch skipped on this host; no Linux native qualification inferred.
Go full-suite evidence is contextual regression coverage for unchanged Go sources; isolated focused gates carry the exact evaluated-Subject binding.
Skill execution was explicitly loaded; automatic discovery behavior was not measured.

Named-test evidence can still be fabricated by a test binary that controls its own stdout and branches on -test.list; the derived go test -list cross-check (F5) raises the cost of silent forgery, and the independent diff review remains the guard.

Session metadata exports safe-token identifiers verbatim unless they are path-like (then hashed); a secret shaped like an ordinary token is not distinguishable by shape, so operators must never pass credential, prompt or transcript values.

An export with no assistant messages, no observed prompt hash or no timestamps, or an assistant identity missing provider/api, cannot be imported as a model row and must be recorded as explicit non-model evidence (runbook mapping); the importer is not relaxed to accept these shapes.
